title: Org governance toggles: IP whitelist, sharing lockdown, export shield
creator: Asha Patel
description: Add a cohesive set of org-level governance toggles that allow security teams to: 1) enforce an IP allowlist for Console/API access, 2) disable public sharing for assets (links / share-to-external), and 3) hard-disable data exports for sensitive orgs. This ticket scopes the runtime + control-plane enforcement model, RBAC v2 integration, audit logging schema for toggle events, and console UX surface. The goal is to provide a single source-of-truth toggle per org that is honored across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. We must avoid redundant enforcement paths that create inconsistent behaviors across model serving or export flows.
acceptance_criteria: Org toggle exists in Control Plane and can be set via Console and Admin API
Toggle decisions are enforced at the earliest gate (authz middleware) for Console/API and at data-plane export endpoints for exports
Audit log record emitted for every toggle change with actor, method (console/api/saml), previous and new state, and request_id
RBAC v2 respects toggle: non-admins cannot override enforcement; service accounts with 'export.bypass' must be explicitly granted
E2E tests cover Hosted, Dedicated, Private flows and fail when export attempted while export shield enabled
Console shows toggle state, last-modified-by, and link to policy docs
Performance regression <= 3% p95 request latency attributable to new authz checks

notes: Trade-offs considered: enforcing only in control plane is faster to ship but risks bypass in edge Dedicated/on-prem flows; full data-plane enforcement increases changeset size and testing matrix.
Decision: implement both control-plane gating and data-plane enforcement for export and sharing endpoints. Provide 'export.bypass' RBAC permission for service accounts with explicit audit trail.
Implementation detail: audit log will store raw payload diff for toggle changes truncated to 8KB and a reference to full change artifact stored in S3 for forensic needs.
SSO/SAML: Provisioned SAML attributes should map to RBAC groups; admin-level SAML assertion changes must be logged as 'method=saml' and require MFA per policy.
